subject.title: feat(gateway): idempotent start, non-interactive stop guard, unified lifecycle audit

question: Should repository-owned unattended lifecycle and release checks explicitly opt into `gateway stop --force`, or should the new non-interactive policy exempt a defined trusted automation boundary?
rationale: The PR deliberately changes operator-safety semantics, but existing owned automation relies on the previous unguarded stop behavior; choosing the permanent trust boundary is a maintainer policy decision.

options.title: Update owned automation to opt in
options.body: Pass `--force` only at reviewed repository-owned stop call sites that intentionally mutate the managed Gateway, while retaining the safe default elsewhere.

options.title: Define a narrow trusted exemption
options.body: Preserve unguarded behavior only for a documented, narrowly scoped automation pathway and add tests proving it cannot be used by ordinary unattended callers.

recommendation.title: Update owned automation to opt in
recommendation.body: Pass `--force` only at reviewed repository-owned stop call sites that intentionally mutate the managed Gateway, while retaining the safe default elsewhere.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the assigned recent contributor for the Gateway lifecycle policy and can route the intended automation boundary for review.
